title: The Twins' Death and Return
subtitle: A staged death outwits Xibalba's rulers

fate.excerpt: The monarchs of Xibalba, anxious to experience the novel sensation of a temporary death, requested to be slain and resuscitated. They were speedily killed, but the brothers refrained from resuscitating their arch-enemies.

narrativeBlocks.title: The death they choose
narrativeBlocks.body: Out-tricked at every turn, the lords summon the twins to one last pyre — and the twins, knowing it, leap in willingly: they are burned, ground, and scattered on the river.

narrativeBlocks.title: Ashes into catfish
narrativeBlocks.body: From the river the ashes become catfish — then the twins themselves, returned disguised as wandering beggar-dancers.

narrativeBlocks.title: The dance that kills the lords
narrativeBlocks.body: Their show-stopper trick: they 'sacrifice' each other and restore one another — the lords, delighted, ask to be sacrificed too — and the twins sacrifice them for real, without the restoration.

narrativeBlocks.title: The lords' defeat
narrativeBlocks.body: One by one the death-lords of Xibalba are destroyed — the twins win the underworld by the very trick the lords taught them: sacrifice.

narrativeBlocks.title: Through Spence's summary
narrativeBlocks.body: We reach this tale through Lewis Spence's summary of the Popol Vuh — a secondary retelling of the Quiche Maya book, not the text itself — the story is real, the voice is an intermediary.

quiz.prompt: How do the twins defeat the lords of Xibalba?

choices.text: They storm Xibalba with an army
They let themselves be sacrificed and return disguised — then 'sacrifice' the lords in their own show-trick, without restoring them
They bargain for the lords' surrender

quiz.explanation: The final trick flips the sacrifice on the sacrificers.

quiz.prompt: What form do the twins take after being burned?

choices.text: Their ashes become catfish in the river — then the twins returned as beggar-dancers
They become birds in the sky

quiz.explanation: Death → ashes → catfish → beggars → gods of the story.
